prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Miami for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car-accident case in Miami — the right attorney depends on your priorities (trial experience vs. quick settlement), the severity/complexity of your injuries, whether the other driver is uninsured, whether there are complicated medical-liens or catastrophic injuries, and your budget or language needs.

How to find the best lawyer for your case
- Look for experience with car-accident cases and trial experience (not just settlements).  
- Check credentials: Florida Bar standing, years practicing, and whether they’re board-certified in civil trial law or personal injury (if applicable).  
- Review results: past settlements/verdicts in similar cases (especially for similar injuries).  
- Read client reviews on Google, Avvo, Super Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell, and local forums.  
- Ask about fees and costs (most PI lawyers work on contingency — typically about 33%–40% of the recovery plus expenses).  
- Confirm communication style, points of contact, and how they handle medical liens and treatment coordination.  
- Get references or ask to speak with recent clients if possible.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- How many car-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?  
- Have you handled cases with injuries like mine (neck/back, TBI, fractures)? Outcomes?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (attorney or paralegal)?  
- What do you estimate my case is worth and why?  
- What percentage do you charge and what costs will I be responsible for if we don’t recover?  
- How long do you expect it to take?  
- How will you keep me updated?

Practical items & timing
- Florida’s statute of limitations for most personal-injury claims is 4 years from the accident date — don’t wait to consult an attorney.  
- Preserve evidence: photos, medical records, police report, witness contacts, and insurance information.

How I can help next
If you want, tell me your Miami zip code, a brief summary of the accident/injuries, and any preferences (e.g., Spanish-speaking, trial-focused, small firm vs. large firm). I can then provide a short list (3–5) of highly-rated Miami personal-injury attorneys/firms and links to their profiles so you can set up consultations.
